newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Podravka cuts share price, issues shares.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Podravka cuts share price, issues shares.

text.p: Croatian food processor Podravka on Friday cut the face value of its shares to 300 kuna and reduced its equity, but boosted reserves some 314 million kuna.
At an annual meeting, Podravka's shareholders also approved a new third issue, totalling 171,450 shares, which raised its total number of shares to 5.4 million.

They were alloted to government institutions that control 60 percent in the company in lieu of their 51.4 million kuna unpaid 1993 dividend. Before this move, Podravka's shares rose 260 kuna on the Zagreb Stock Exchange.
After expressing its share price in kuna in accordance with the new company law and adjusting it for the exchange rate difference, Podravka cut its equity to 1.62 billion kuna.
Podravka was valued at 523.5 million German marks, or 1.99 billion kuna, in 1993 and split into 5.23 million shares.

Each had a face value of 100 marks, the equivalent of 380 kuna, but have since lost some 26 kuna in nominal terms as the domestic currency appreciated. Podravka made a 1995 loss of 135 million kuna on the group level to be covered by reserves. The company will sell some of its loss-making subsidiaries and hopes to turn a profit by 1997 if not this year.
